brief.situation: You are a junior analyst in the security operations team at Fenwick Logistics, a fictional freight company. At 09:00 four alerts wait in the queue. Triage them, decide which is an incident, follow the incident response plan, and write it up.
handover: The incident response plan says: an analyst who confirms an incident declares it and pages the incident handler; the phishing playbook lets an analyst reset a password, revoke sessions, block a sender and pull messages.
Severity labels come from the tools, not from what is happening.
howItWorks: Each task takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. An attacker, if there is one, works on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen.
When you close the incident you notify, record it and explain your reasoning.

source.note: Fifteen minutes until the attacker sets a forwarding rule is the author's figure.
Twenty-five minutes until the internal phishing email is the author's figure.
Fifteen minutes until a colleague enters a password on the internal phish is the author's figure.
Forty-five minutes until the supplier bank details are changed is the author's figure.
Declaring within 15 minutes of the alerts is the author's teaching figure; the plan in the brief asks for a declaration once an incident is confirmed.

writeup.question: For the incident record: how you triaged the queue, why you declared what you declared, and what you did about the people involved.

parts.label: Triage
parts.criteria: Ranks by what is happening, not the tool's label: correlates the user report with the sign-in (same user, minutes apart) as the incident, and closes the blocked firewall traffic and the scheduled antivirus test on evidence.
parts.modelAnswer: The low-labelled sign-in and the user report were one event: her password used from 192.0.2.77 minutes after she typed it in. The firewall drops and the EICAR test were noise I closed with notes.

parts.label: Plan
parts.criteria: Declares the incident and pages the handler as the plan says; resets and revokes, removes the forwarding rule, keeps the message and log before pulling copies.
parts.modelAnswer: I declared it and paged the handler, ran the playbook (reset, revoke, rule removed), saved the email and log, then pulled every copy and blocked the domain.

parts.label: People
parts.criteria: Treats the reporting user as an ally, not a culprit; warns staff; notifies only the handler and manager.
parts.modelAnswer: a.lind reported it, which is what we want people to do; I warned staff with the awareness team's message and told only the handler and her manager.

expertPath.text: Correlate: the user report and the 'low' sign-in are one person, minutes apart. That is the incident.
Declare it and page the handler; reset and revoke; check for forwarding rules.
Save the email and log, block the sender, pull every copy, warn staff.
Close the firewall drops and the scheduled antivirus test with notes; record credential phishing; tell the handler and her manager.

handled.headline: Good: correlated, declared, contained
handled.body: The tool's labels pointed the wrong way. Correlating by user and time found the one real incident, and the plan did the rest.

handledLate.headline: Contained, with gaps
handledLate.body: The account is closed. The criteria show what cost you: a late declaration, the internal phish going out, or evidence saved late.

fraud.headline: The fraud came first
fraud.body: Working the queue by its labels left the stolen password working for 45 minutes. Correlate before you sort.

evidenceLost.headline: Evidence pulled with the mail
evidenceLost.body: Save one copy with its headers before you pull the rest; the plan's data handling rules exist for this.

leftOpen.headline: A way in was left open
leftOpen.body: A reset without a session revoke, or a forwarding rule left behind, keeps the attacker in after the queue is clear.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No incident record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Triage by what is happening, not by the label. The user report and the new-country sign-in are the same person minutes apart: credential phishing with a live session, the incident use case in this queue. Declare it under the plan and page the handler, reset the password and revoke sessions, check for forwarding rules, save the email with headers and the sign-in log, then block the sender, pull every copy and warn staff. The firewall drops (blocked, port closed) and the EICAR alert (a scheduled test) are closed with notes. The user who reported it is an ally.
